audit.whatIsWrong: whys[0] said 'Level 1 is yours' while win[0] and phases[0].side both read Akshan; whys[4] said 'Level 6 is yours' while win[4] and phases[4].side both read Akshan.
audit.why: The row and its explanation render together, so the page answered its own question twice, differently.
audit.corrected: whys[0] and whys[4] rewritten to Akshan's side, matching both layers. Sides left untouched — full and content agree row for row.

audit.whatIsWrong: Primal Howl appears nowhere in the entry, and no cooldowns are given.
audit.why: Mirror finding on akshan__warwick: Primal Howl is the ability that most directly answers a poke-and-burst laner — 2.5s of damage reduction then a 1s fear, 15s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: Primal Howl's 2.5s damage reduction and 1s fear written into early; Comeuppance's missing-health scaling written into phases[4].why and mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: TWO fabrications, each repeated. (1) 'R Infinite Duress is unstoppable' — it is not; the kit carries the channel flag, so CC on Warwick breaks the suppression. (2) 'Blood Hunt reveals him' / 'keeps him revealed' — Blood Hunt grants move speed toward and attack speed against sub-50% enemies and nothing else. It gives no vision. Stated in spikes[1], spikes[3], late and wants.you[2].
audit.why: Riot's W text has no reveal component; Riot's R text is a directional leap and the derived flags mark it interruptible.
audit.corrected: 'Unstoppable' replaced with the true caveat that CC on you breaks the suppression; the invented reveal replaced with the real interaction from the mirror — Infinite Duress leaps further the more bonus move speed Warwick has, so Blood Hunt lengthens the leap.

audit.why: Heroic Swing at 18s rank 1 is correctly held as the punishable window and the entry already builds around it.

edits.before: Level 1 is yours since your Q sustain beats Akshan before his W/E combo is online.
edits.after: Level 1 is Akshan's: Avengerang out-ranges you before Jaws of the Beast is online.

edits.before: Level 6 is yours: R Infinite Duress is unstoppable and cancels his Heroic Swing.
edits.after: Level 6 goes to Akshan: Comeuppance punishes you low and CC breaks your R.

edits.before: Your R Infinite Duress is unstoppable and locks him mid-air, cancelling any Heroic Swing reposition; all-in at 6 when Blood Hunt reveals him after his E dash.
edits.after: Infinite Duress suppresses him mid-swing and cancels the Heroic Swing reposition, but CC on you breaks it — Blood Hunt's move speed also makes the leap travel further.

edits.before: Even late your R hard-catches his low-HP frame; force fights in tight terrain where his E swing anchor is limited and Blood Hunt keeps him revealed.
edits.after: Even late your R catches his low-HP frame; fight in tight terrain where he has no swing anchor, and Blood Hunt's bonus move speed lengthens the leap.

edits.before: You stay favoured into items because Akshan is fragile and your R reliably catches his low-HP frame through his mobility; fight in tight terrain and use Blood Hunt to keep him revealed after every dash.
edits.after: You stay favoured into items because Akshan is fragile and your R catches his low-HP frame through his mobility; fight in tight terrain, and let Blood Hunt's move speed stretch the leap onto him.

edits.before: Use W reveal after his E dash to chase and finish
edits.after: Let Blood Hunt speed stretch your R leap onto him

edits.before: The level-3 to level-5 window is skill-dependent as you close range through minions against his kiting, but level 6 flips hard to you: R Infinite Duress is unstoppable and cancels Heroic Swing, so all-in on cooldown.
edits.after: The level-3 to level-5 window is skill-dependent as you close range through minions against his kiting, but at 6 respect Comeuppance: Infinite Duress cancels Heroic Swing, yet any CC on you breaks the suppression.

edits.before: Level 1 is yours with Q sustain, but Akshan's level-2 W/E combo gives him a poke-and-reposition window where his range and passive shield out-trade you — respect that spike, then look to walk him down once you hit 3.
edits.after: Akshan's Avengerang out-ranges you at 1, and his level-2 poke plus passive shield out-trades you — hold Primal Howl for his step-up: 2.5s of damage reduction, then a 1s fear, and walk him down once you hit 3.

edits.before: Infinite Duress is a point-and-click fight starter that locks his carry tool. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Akshan's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Infinite Duress is a directional leap, not point-and-click, and CC on you breaks it. Comeuppance scales on your missing health — never fight it low.

edits.before: Infinite Duress is a point-and-click fight starter that locks his carry tool — build your teamfight around that. Akshan carry threat: 7.5/10 — shift to picks and wave control if he gets ahead.
edits.after: Infinite Duress is a directional leap that suppresses the first champion it collides with — build the fight around it. Akshan carry threat: 7.5/10 — shift to picks and wave control if he gets ahead.

notes: Two repeated fabrications killed: Infinite Duress described as 'unstoppable' (the kit marks it a channel — CC on Warwick breaks the suppression), and Blood Hunt described as revealing Akshan (it grants move and attack speed only, no vision). Replaced the fake reveal with the real, mirror-confirmed interaction: Infinite Duress leaps further the more bonus move speed Warwick has, so Blood Hunt extends its range.
